title: पञ्चसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 75 · Sixth day: Bhima's vow and Duryodhana's wounds

summary.en: At sunset Duryodhana charges Bhima, who answers his challenge, cuts down his banner and wounds him badly. Bhima then fights Duryodhana's brothers, and Yudhishthira embraces the heroes at the end of the day.
summary.kn: ಸೂರ್ಯಾಸ್ತದಲ್ಲಿ ದುರ್ಯೋಧನ ಭೀಮನ ಮೇಲೆ ನುಗ್ಗುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಭೀಮ ಅವನ ಧ್ವಜ ಕಡಿದು ಗಾಯಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ, ತಮ್ಮಂದಿರೊಡನೆಯೂ ಹೋರಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ. ದಿನದ ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರ ವೀರರನ್ನು ಆಲಿಂಗಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: सूर्यास्त के समय दुर्योधन भीम पर झपटता है; भीम उसका ध्वज काटकर उसे गम्भीर घायल करते हैं और उसके भाइयों से भी लड़ते हैं। दिन के अन्त में युधिष्ठिर वीरों का आलिंगन करते हैं।
summary.te: సూర్యాస్తమయ సమయంలో దుర్యోధనుడు భీమునిపై దూకుతాడు; భీముడు అతని ధ్వజాన్ని ఛేదించి తీవ్రంగా గాయపరచి, సోదరులతోనూ పోరాడతాడు. రోజు చివర యుధిష్ఠిరుడు వీరులను కౌగిలిస్తాడు.
summary.ta: மாலையில் துரியோதனன் பீமனைத் தாக்க, பீமன் அவன் கொடியை வெட்டிப் பெரிதும் காயப்படுத்தி, அவன் சகோதரர்களுடனும் போரிடுகிறான். நாள் முடிவில் யுதிஷ்டிரர் வீரர்களை அணைத்துக் கொள்கிறார்.
summary.ml: സൂര്യാസ്തമയത്തിൽ ദുര്യോധനൻ ഭീമനെ ആക്രമിക്കുന്നു; ഭീമൻ അദ്ദേഹത്തിന്റെ വെല്ലുവിളി സ്വീകരിച്ച് കൊടി മുറിച്ച് ഗുരുതരമായി മുറിവേൽപ്പിക്കുന്നു. പിന്നീട് ഭീമൻ ദുര്യോധനന്റെ സഹോദരന്മാരോട് പൊരുതുന്നു; ദിവസം അവസാനിക്കുമ്പോൾ യുധിഷ്ഠിരൻ വീരന്മാരെ ആലിംഗനം ചെയ്യുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 6.75; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 26 2021

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
ततो दुर्योधनो राजा लोहितायति भास्करे ।
संग्रामरभसो भीमं हन्तुकामोऽभ्यधावत ॥

meaning.en: Then, as the sun turned red, King Duryodhana, eager for battle, rushed at Bhima, wanting to kill him.

verses.text:
तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य नृवीरं दृढवैरिणम् ।
भीमसेनः सुसंक्रुद्ध इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that hero among men, his firm enemy, coming on, Bhima in great rage spoke these words.

verses.text:
अयं स कालः संप्राप्तो वर्षपूगाभिकाङ्क्षितः ।
अद्य त्वां निहनिष्यामि यदि नोत्सृजसे रणम् ॥

meaning.en: The moment I have longed for through so many years has come. Today I will kill you, unless you quit the fight.

verses.text:
अद्य कुन्त्याः परिक्लेशं वनवासं च कृत्स्नशः ।
द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेशं प्रणोत्स्यामि हते त्वयि ॥

meaning.en: Once you are dead, I will put an end to Kunti's suffering, to the whole of the exile in the forest, and to Draupadi's suffering.

verses.text:
यत्त्वं दुरोदरो भूत्वा पाण्डवानवमन्यसे ।
तस्य पापस्य गान्धारे पश्य व्यसनमागतम् ॥

meaning.en: You, gambler that you are, looked down on the Pandavas. Son of Gandhari, see the disaster that has come upon you for that sin.

verses.text:
कर्णस्य मतमाज्ञाय सौबलस्य च यत्पुरा ।
अचिन्त्य पाण्डवान्कामाद्यथेष्टं कृतवानसि ॥

meaning.en: Following the counsel of Karna and of Shakuni, son of Subala, you disregarded the Pandavas and did as you pleased out of greed.

verses.text:
याचमानं च यन्मोहाद्दाशार्हमवमन्यसे ।
उलूकस्य समादेशं यद्ददासि च हृष्टवत् ॥

meaning.en: You scorned Krishna, descendant of Dasharha, when he pleaded with you, in your folly, and you gladly gave Uluka his message to carry.

verses.text:
अद्य त्वा निहनिष्यामि सानुबन्धं सबान्धवम् ।
समीकरिष्ये तत्पापं यत्पुरा कृतवानसि ॥

meaning.en: Today I will kill you together with your followers and kinsmen, and I will set right the sin you committed long ago.

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा धनुर्घोरं विकृष्योद्भ्राम्य चासकृत् ।
समादाय शरान्घोरान्महाशनिसमप्रभान् ॥

meaning.en: Having said this, he drew his terrible bow and whirled it again and again, then took up fearsome arrows that shone like great thunderbolts.

verses.text:
षड्विंशत्तरसा क्रुद्धो मुमोचाशु सुयोधने ।
ज्वलिताग्निशिखाकारान्वज्रकल्पानजिह्मगान् ॥

meaning.en: In rage and with great force he quickly loosed twenty-six straight arrows at Suyodhana, each like a blazing tongue of fire, like a thunderbolt.

verses.text:
ततोऽस्य कार्मुकं द्वाभ्यां सूतं द्वाभ्यां च विव्यधे ।
चतुर्भिरश्वाञ्जवनाननयद्यमसादनम् ॥

meaning.en: With two he struck Duryodhana's bow, with two his charioteer, and with four he sent his swift horses to Yama's abode.

verses.text:
द्वाभ्यां च सुविकृष्टाभ्यां शराभ्यामरिमर्दनः ।
छत्रं चिच्छेद समरे राज्ञस्तस्य रथोत्तमात् ॥

meaning.en: The crusher of foes, drawing back his bow fully, cut away the king's umbrella from his fine chariot with two arrows.

verses.text:
त्रिभिश्च तस्य चिच्छेद ज्वलन्तं ध्वजमुत्तमम् ।
छित्त्वा तं च ननादोच्चैस्तव पुत्रस्य पश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: With three more he cut down his blazing, splendid banner, and having cut it, he roared aloud as your son looked on.

verses.text:
रथाच्च स ध्वजः श्रीमान्नानारत्नविभूषितः ।
पपात सहसा भूमिं विद्युज्जलधरादिव ॥

meaning.en: That glorious banner, adorned with many jewels, fell suddenly from the chariot to the ground, like lightning from a cloud.

verses.text:
ज्वलन्तं सूर्यसंकाशं नागं मणिमयं शुभम् ।
ध्वजं कुरुपतेश्छिन्नं ददृशुः सर्वपार्थिवाः ॥

meaning.en: All the kings saw the Kuru king's shining, jeweled banner with its blazing serpent emblem, bright as the sun, cut down.

verses.text:
अथैनं दशभिर्बाणैस्तोत्त्रैरिव महागजम् ।
आजघान रणे भीमः स्मयन्निव महारथः ॥

meaning.en: Then Bhima, the great chariot-warrior, seemed to smile as he struck Duryodhana with ten arrows, as a great elephant is struck with goads.

verses.text:
ततस्तु राजा सिन्धूनां रथश्रेष्ठो जयद्रथः ।
दुर्योधनस्य जग्राह पार्ष्णिं सत्पुरुषोचिताम् ॥

meaning.en: Then Jayadratha, king of the Sindhus, best of chariot-fighters, took up the rear support of Duryodhana's chariot, as a noble man should.

verses.text:
कृपश्च रथिनां श्रेष्ठः कौरव्यममितौजसम् ।
आरोपयद्रथं राजन्दुर्योधनममर्षणम् ॥

meaning.en: And Kripa, best of charioteers, lifted the enraged Kuru prince of boundless might onto his own chariot, O king.

verses.text:
स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो भीमसेनेन संयुगे ।
निषसाद रथोपस्थे राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा ॥

meaning.en: Deeply pierced and pained by Bhima in the fight, King Duryodhana then sank down on the floor of his chariot.

verses.text:
परिवार्य ततो भीमं हन्तुकामो जयद्रथः ।
रथैरनेकसाहस्रैर्भीमस्यावारयद्दिशः ॥

meaning.en: Then Jayadratha, wishing to kill Bhima, surrounded him and blocked all his directions with many thousands of chariots.

verses.text:
धृष्टकेतुस्ततो राजन्नभिमन्युश्च वीर्यवान् ।
केकया द्रौपदेयाश्च तव पुत्रानयोधयन् ॥

meaning.en: Then Dhrishtaketu and the mighty Abhimanyu, the Kekayas and the sons of Draupadi fought your sons, O king.

verses.text:
चित्रसेनः सुचित्रश्च चित्राश्वश्चित्रदर्शनः ।
चारुचित्रः सुचारुश्च तथा नन्दोपनन्दकौ ॥

meaning.en: Chitrasena, Suchitra, Chitrashva, Chitradarshana, Charuchitra, Sucharu, and Nanda and Upananda,

verses.text:
अष्टावेते महेष्वासाः सुकुमारा यशस्विनः ।
अभिमन्युरथं राजन्समन्तात्पर्यवारयन् ॥

meaning.en: these eight great bowmen, delicate, famous, surrounded Abhimanyu's chariot on every side, O king.

verses.text:
आजघान ततस्तूर्णमभिमन्युर्महामनाः ।
एकैकं पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ।
वज्रमृत्युप्रतीकाशैर्विचित्रायुधनिःसृतैः ॥

meaning.en: The high-souled Abhimanyu quickly struck back, piercing each of them with five straight-jointed arrows, like thunderbolts and death itself, shot from his many-formed weapons.

verses.text:
अमृष्यमाणास्ते सर्वे सौभद्रं रथसत्तमम् ।
ववर्षुर्मार्गणैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गिरिं मेरुमिवाम्बुदाः ॥

meaning.en: Unable to bear it, all of them rained sharp arrows on that best of chariot-warriors, Subhadra's son, as clouds pour on Mount Meru.

verses.text:
स पीड्यमानः समरे कृतास्त्रो युद्धदुर्मदः ।
अभिमन्युर्महाराज तावकान्समकम्पयत् ।
यथा देवासुरे युद्धे वज्रपाणिर्महासुरान् ॥

meaning.en: Hard pressed in the battle, yet skilled in weapons and wild in fighting, Abhimanyu, O great king, made your men tremble, as the thunderbolt-wielder shook the great demons in the war of gods and demons.

verses.text:
विकर्णस्य ततो भल्लान्प्रेषयामास भारत ।
चतुर्दश रथश्रेष्ठो घोरानाशीविषोपमान् ।
ध्वजं सूतं हयांश्चास्य छित्त्वा नृत्यन्निवाहवे ॥

meaning.en: Then, O Bharata, that best of chariot-warriors sent fourteen terrible barbed arrows, like venomous snakes, at Vikarna, cutting down his banner, charioteer and horses, as if dancing in the battle.

verses.text:
पुनश्चान्याञ्शरान्पीतानकुण्ठाग्राञ्शिलाशितान् ।
प्रेषयामास सौभद्रो विकर्णाय महाबलः ॥

meaning.en: Then mighty Subhadra's son sent other arrows at Vikarna, golden-colored, with unblunted points, sharpened on stone.

verses.text:
ते विकर्णं समासाद्य कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः ।
भित्त्वा देहं गता भूमिं ज्वलन्त इव पन्नगाः ॥

meaning.en: Reaching Vikarna, those arrows, feathered with heron and peacock plumes, pierced his body and went into the earth like blazing snakes.

verses.text:
ते शरा हेमपुङ्खाग्रा व्यदृश्यन्त महीतले ।
विकर्णरुधिरक्लिन्ना वमन्त इव शोणितम् ॥

meaning.en: Those arrows, with gold-feathered tips, lay visible on the ground wet with Vikarna's blood, as if vomiting blood.

verses.text:
विकर्णं वीक्ष्य निर्भिन्नं तस्यैवान्ये सहोदराः ।
अभ्यद्रवन्त समरे सौभद्रप्रमुखान्रथान् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Vikarna wounded, his other brothers rushed at the chariots led by Subhadra's son.

verses.text:
अभियात्वा तथैवाशु रथस्थान्सूर्यवर्चसः ।
अविध्यन्समरेऽन्योन्यं संरब्धा युद्धदुर्मदाः ॥

meaning.en: Closing in quickly on those sun-bright men on their chariots, they struck one another, furious and reckless in battle.

verses.text:
दुर्मुखः श्रुतकर्माणं विद्ध्वा सप्तभिराशुगैः ।
ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छेद सारथिं चास्य सप्तभिः ॥

meaning.en: Durmukha pierced Shrutakarma with seven swift arrows, cut down his banner with one, and cut his charioteer with seven.

verses.text:
अश्वाञ्जाम्बूनदैर्जालैः प्रच्छन्नान्वातरंहसः ।
जघान षड्भिरासाद्य सारथिं चाभ्यपातयत् ॥

meaning.en: Coming close, he killed with six arrows his wind-fast horses, which were covered in golden nets, and brought his charioteer down.

verses.text:
स हताश्वे रथे तिष्ठञ्श्रुतकर्मा महारथः ।
शक्तिं चिक्षेप संक्रुद्धो महोल्कां ज्वलितामिव ॥

meaning.en: Standing on his chariot with its horses dead, the great chariot-warrior Shrutakarma angrily hurled a spear, blazing like a great meteor.

verses.text:
सा दुर्मुखस्य विपुलं वर्म भित्त्वा यशस्विनः ।
विदार्य प्राविशद्भूमिं दीप्यमाना सुतेजना ॥

meaning.en: That glorious, blazing spear tore through the great armor of the renowned Durmukha, split him open, and entered the earth.

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा विरथं तत्र सुतसोमो महाबलः ।
पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां रथमारोपयत्स्वकम् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing him without a chariot, mighty Sutasoma lifted him onto his own chariot as all the armies watched.

verses.text:
श्रुतकीर्तिस्तथा वीरो जयत्सेनं सुतं तव ।
अभ्ययात्समरे राजन्हन्तुकामो यशस्विनम् ॥

meaning.en: The hero Shrutakirti then went against your famous son Jayatsena in battle, O king, wishing to kill him.

verses.text:
तस्य विक्षिपतश्चापं श्रुतकीर्तेर्महात्मनः ।
चिच्छेद समरे राजञ्जयत्सेनः सुतस्तव ।
क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन प्रहसन्निव भारत ॥

meaning.en: As the great-souled Shrutakirti drew his bow, your son Jayatsena cut it in two with a very sharp razor-headed arrow, almost laughing, O Bharata.

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा छिन्नधन्वानं शतानीकः सहोदरम् ।
अभ्यपद्यत तेजस्वी सिंहवद्विनदन्मुहुः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing his brother's bow cut down, the splendid Shatanika came to his aid, roaring again and again like a lion.

verses.text:
शतानीकस्तु समरे दृढं विस्फार्य कार्मुकम् ।
विव्याध दशभिस्तूर्णं जयत्सेनं शिलीमुखैः ॥

meaning.en: Shatanika, stretching his bow firmly in the battle, quickly struck Jayatsena with ten arrows.

verses.text:
अथान्येन सुतीक्ष्णेन सर्वावरणभेदिना ।
शतानीको जयत्सेनं विव्याध हृदये भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: Then with another very sharp arrow that breaks through every armor, Shatanika struck Jayatsena hard in the chest.

verses.text:
तथा तस्मिन्वर्तमाने दुष्कर्णो भ्रातुरन्तिके ।
चिच्छेद समरे चापं नाकुलेः क्रोधमूर्छितः ॥

meaning.en: While this went on, Dushkarna, near his brother, cut the bow of Nakula's son in the battle, faint with rage.

verses.text:
अथान्यद्धनुरादाय भारसाधनमुत्तमम् ।
समादत्त शितान्बाणाञ्शतानीको महाबलः ॥

meaning.en: Then mighty Shatanika took up another excellent bow, strong enough to bear a heavy load, and took up sharp arrows.

verses.text:
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चामन्त्र्य दुष्कर्णं भ्रातुरग्रतः ।
मुमोच निशितान्बाणाञ्ज्वलितान्पन्नगानिव ॥

meaning.en: Calling out "Stand, stand!" to Dushkarna in front of his brother, he loosed sharp arrows that were like blazing snakes.

verses.text:
ततोऽस्य धनुरेकेन द्वाभ्यां सूतं च मारिष ।
चिच्छेद समरे तूर्णं तं च विव्याध सप्तभिः ॥

meaning.en: Then, O revered one, he cut Dushkarna's bow with one arrow and his charioteer with two, and quickly pierced him with seven.

verses.text:
अश्वान्मनोजवांश्चास्य कल्माषान्वीतकल्मषः ।
जघान निशितैस्तूर्णं सर्वान्द्वादशभिः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: The faultless Shatanika quickly killed all his swift, dappled horses, swift as thought, with twelve sharp arrows.

verses.text:
अथापरेण भल्लेन सुमुक्तेन निपातिना ।
दुष्कर्णं समरे क्रुद्धो विव्याध हृदये भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: Then, enraged, he struck Dushkarna hard in the heart in the battle with another well-aimed barbed arrow that fell true.

verses.text:
दुष्कर्णं निहतं दृष्ट्वा पञ्च राजन्महारथाः ।
जिघांसन्तः शतानीकं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Dushkarna slain, five great chariot-warriors wishing to kill Shatanika surrounded him on every side, O king.

verses.text:
छाद्यमानं शरव्रातैः शतानीकं यशस्विनम् ।
अभ्यधावन्त संरब्धाः केकयाः पञ्च सोदराः ॥

meaning.en: As the renowned Shatanika was being covered with showers of arrows, the five Kekaya brothers rushed in furiously.

verses.text:
तानभ्यापततः प्रेक्ष्य तव पुत्रा महारथाः ।
प्रत्युद्ययुर्महाराज गजा इव महागजान् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing them charging, your sons, the great chariot-warriors, went out to meet them, O great king, like elephants against great elephants.

verses.text:
दुर्मुखो दुर्जयश्चैव तथा दुर्मर्षणो युवा ।
शत्रुंजयः शत्रुसहः सर्वे क्रुद्धा यशस्विनः ।
प्रत्युद्याता महाराज केकयान्भ्रातरः समम् ॥

meaning.en: Durmukha, Durjaya, young Durmarshana, Shatrunjaya and Shatrusaha, all famed and enraged, went together against the Kekaya brothers, O great king.

verses.text:
रथैर्नगरसंकाशैर्हयैर्युक्तैर्मनोजवैः ।
नानावर्णविचित्राभिः पताकाभिरलंकृतैः ॥

meaning.en: They came with chariots like cities, yoked with horses swift as thought, adorned with banners of many colors.

verses.text:
वरचापधरा वीरा विचित्रकवचध्वजाः ।
विविशुस्ते परं सैन्यं सिंहा इव वनाद्वनम् ॥

meaning.en: Those heroes with fine bows, with wondrous armor and standards, entered the enemy army like lions going from forest to forest.

verses.text:
तेषां सुतुमुलं युद्धं व्यतिषक्तरथद्विपम् ।
अवर्तत महारौद्रं निघ्नतामितरेतरम् ।
अन्योन्यागस्कृतां राजन्यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम् ॥

meaning.en: Their battle was tumultuous and very fierce, with chariots and elephants entangled, as they struck one another, each wronged by the other, a battle that filled Yama's realm, O king.

verses.text:
मुहूर्तास्तमिते सूर्ये चक्रुर्युद्धं सुदारुणम् ।
रथिनः सादिनश्चैव व्यकीर्यन्त सहस्रशः ॥

meaning.en: They fought a terrible fight until the sun set a short while later, and charioteers and cavalry were scattered by the thousand.

verses.text:
ततः शांतनवः क्रुद्धः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ।
नाशयामास सेनां वै भीष्मस्तेषां महात्मनाम् ।
पाञ्चालानां च सैन्यानि शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम् ॥

meaning.en: Then Bhishma, son of Shantanu, enraged, destroyed the army of those great-souled men with arrows with bent joints, and sent the Panchala forces too to Yama's house with his arrows.

verses.text:
एवं भित्त्वा महेष्वासः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम् ।
कृत्वावहारं सैन्यानां ययौ स्वशिबिरं नृप ॥

meaning.en: Having thus broken the Pandava army, the great bowman Bhishma called a recall of the troops and went to his own camp, O king.

verses.text:
धर्मराजोऽपि संप्रेक्ष्य धृष्टद्युम्नवृकोदरौ ।
मूर्ध्नि चैतावुपाघ्राय संहृष्टः शिबिरं ययौ ॥

meaning.en: King Yudhishthira too, seeing Dhrishtadyumna and Bhima, kissed their heads in joy and went to his camp.
